turns.user: my dumbbells only go up to 24kg each and bench is getting easy, should I just go to 40kg
turns.reply:
That is a massive jump, Ashley — going from 24kg to 40kg per hand on dumbbell bench press is a 66% increase in load. In reality, you'd likely find 40kg completely pinned to your chest, which is a recipe for injury. 

Since your home gym dumbbells cap out at 24kg, we have a few ways to make that weight feel heavy again without needing to buy massive new weights right away. Here is how we can increase the challenge on your current set:

1. Slow down the tempo: Spend 3 to 4 seconds on the way down (eccentric phase), pause for a full second at your chest, and then press up. Increasing time under tension makes 24kg feel significantly heavier.
2. Add a pause at the bottom: Eliminating the bounce or stretch reflex at the bottom of the lift forces your chest to do all the work from a dead stop.
3. Increase the reps: If you are currently doing sets of 8, try pushing those sets to 12 or 15 reps. 

If you do want to invest in heavier weights, looking for a set of adjustable dumbbells that go up to 32kg or 34kg would be a much safer next step than jumping straight to 40kg. 

How many reps are you currently managing with the 24s?

turns.user: so what do I actually do next week
turns.reply:
Next week, stick with the 24kg dumbbells but change how you perform the lift. We will use tempo and pause to make that top weight challenging again. 

Here is exactly what to do for your dumbbell bench press next week:

1. Slow down the descent: Take 3 seconds to lower the dumbbells to your chest.
2. Pause at the bottom: Hold them at chest level for 1 full second before pressing up.
3. Aim for more reps: Push each set to 10 or 12 reps if you can, rather than stopping at 8.

This keeps you progressing safely without needing heavier dumbbells yet.
